relatedSnapshot.title: Research and fix Conversations unread count mismatch
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Name 1 reported that Conversations shows 2 unread messages while the Unread inbox is empty. His screenshot shows:

* Mine selected, All channels, and no search query.
* Unread 2 and a sidebar Conversations count of 2.
* “Nothing in this inbox” / “You are caught up.”

Original report and screenshot

## Research and fix

* Reproduce by impersonating AIA Sales Team users through the authorized impersonation flow, starting with the reported view and checking more than one user.
* Compare the unread badge/count with the conversations actually returned for the same user and filters.
* Investigate the explanation Foreman posted in the thread: one imported text thread and one imported email thread may be counted as unread, then excluded when the list rechecks live data. Treat this as a lead to verify, not an established root cause.
* Fix the mismatch and check whether existing affected data needs repair.

## Done when

* The unread count and list agree for the same user and filters, including imported Close history and live messages.
* An empty Unread inbox does not retain a nonzero count.
* Reading a conversation updates the count correctly, without changing another user's read state.
* Regression coverage and validation results from AIA Sales Team user impersonation are recorded.

James's request

relatedSnapshot.title: Show authorized text alerts with an exact unread count
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Show authorized inbound-text alerts in today's Notifications panel and publish an exact unread badge through one shared Name 2 owner.

## Problem

The current panel and badge use separate Name 2 clients and approximate unread state. Rendering provider-supplied SMS content can leak stale data after reassignment or access loss, while a custom list can accidentally remove current legacy actions.

## Proposed fix

Use one outer Name 2 provider and one serialized reconciliation owner for badge, list, listeners, pagination, authorization, and mutations. Render SMS content only from stable server hydration and preserve all reachable non-SMS behavior.

## What's included

* Name 4 client, listener set, cache owner, serialized remote lane, and cleanup path per signed-in user.
* Two complete ordered unread-SMS scans plus two identical authorization passes before publishing a count.
* Exact total: all unread non-SMS notifications plus currently authorized unread SMS deliveries.
* Hard invalidation on relevant events, reconnect, offline, cursor gaps, local mutation, user change, or workspace change.
* Complete custom list with bounded pagination, keyed content-free SMS checking rows, hydrated SMS cards, denial removal, and focused-only fallback.
* Preserved legacy subject, body, avatar, time, redirect, primary/secondary actions, mark read/unread, archive, and Snooze whenever the session enables it.
* Reconciliation, provider, list, actions, navigation, focus, listener, cleanup, and badge tests.
* No native notification-store replacement, pop-up, sound, closed-tab push, production enablement, deployment, or pilot.

## Blocked by

* Priority 4: Open inbound text alerts at the exact message.

## How it should work

Listeners attach before the first request. A count appears only after two complete scans have identical ordered IDs, state digests, boundaries, and counts, followed by two identical hydration decisions and fingerprints. Before first convergence the count is pending; after established data becomes uncertain it is unavailable, never a plausible zero. SMS checking state contains no subject, body, avatar, redirect, contact, line, or workspace content. Denial removes the row and unread contribution immediately; focus moves only if that row owned focus. Name 6 and workspace changes clear or invalidate sensitive state.

## Who can do what

The signed-in user can view and mutate only their own Name 2 items. SMS content still requires current server authorization on every accepted reconciliation. Non-SMS behavior remains governed by its current Name 2 workflow and actions.

## What the user sees

Today's panel keeps its current layout and legacy cards. An authorized SMS card shows only hydrated workspace, receiving line, permitted preview, time, and Open conversation. Checking and unavailable states are generic. The badge never shows a partial or stale adjusted total.

## Done when

- [ ] Badge and drawer share exactly one client, listener set, cache, pagination lane, and mutation lane with complete unsubscribe and disconnect cleanup.
- [ ] Stable multi-page scans converge, while same-count swaps, archive replacements, changed delivery IDs, event gaps, reconnects, authorization changes, and cursor repetition cannot publish stale totals.
- [ ] Name 5 SMS subject, body, avatar, and redirect never enter renderable state.
- [ ] Authorized, checking, denied, restored, focused-removal, workspace-change, and logout behavior preserves keyed state without stealing background focus.
- [ ] Every currently reachable non-SMS action and presentation path, including enabled Snooze, remains available and tested.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled. If the installed SDK cannot preserve a current legacy action, stop for scope review.

## Expected outcome

The responsible rep sees safe inbound-text alerts and an exact unread badge in the existing panel without losing current notifications or actions.

## Implementation context

This is priority 5 of five under Notify the responsible rep when a client texts back. It is a bounded current-feed integration adjacent to the future notification store, shared site-wide provider, drawer rebuild, personal preferences and closed-tab push, distinct Conversations-tab unread count, and rollout reconciliation. AI context.md contains the implementation handoff.

relatedSnapshot.title: The unread badge and My Day Replies stay fast with full Close history
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The unread count on the Conversations tab and the Replies card on My Day load quickly for every rep, even after the full Close history is imported into the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace. Today both still rebuild their numbers from all history, so they slow down with every imported call, text and email.

## Problem

Acquisity/Acquisity#6675 moved the main Conversations list and its chip counts onto the ready inbox table (ENG-14372), but deliberately left out the unread badge and My Day Replies. They use an older path that returns one row per thread rather than one per person, and that path is not limited to CRM v2 workspaces. Switching them in the same PR risked hiding the unread badge for workspaces that have My Day but not CRM v2.

Measured on the production replica on 28 Sep, the badge took 2.4 to 3.7 s and the Replies list 2.8 to 4.7 s, and both grow with imported volume. This is one of the paths holding the rest of the Close import (about 94k calls, 430k texts and 790k emails).

## User experience

A rep sees the unread number on the Conversations tab and the Replies card on My Day appear as quickly as the rest of the page. The numbers and rows are the same as today. Workspaces that see the badge or Replies today keep seeing them, including workspaces with My Day but not CRM v2.

## What's included

* The unread badge on the Conversations tab and the My Day Replies card.
* This completes the badge and My Day Replies part of ENG-14372 that PR Acquisity/Acquisity#6675 left out.
* Depends on ENG-14456 so backfilled rows still count as needing a reply.
* Not included: Conversations search, covered by ENG-14464.

## Done when

- [ ] For a sample of users, the badge count and the Replies rows match today's results.
- [ ] Badge and Replies latency is measured on production data for the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace at full Close import volume and stays fast.
- [ ] Workspaces without CRM v2 see no change in whether the badge and Replies appear or what they show.

## Implementation context

* AI context.md: which calls the badge and Replies make today, why PR Acquisity/Acquisity#6675 left them out, the replica measurements and suggested checks.

relatedSnapshot.title: Conversations "Mine" only flags messages that came to you
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

In Conversations, Mine flags a person as Unread or Needs reply whenever they text or email anyone on the team, as long as you were in touch with that person in the last 30 days. Reps who call many leads get flooded with other reps' conversations and can miss the ones that are theirs to answer. Mine should flag a person only when the message came to you, outgoing messages should name who really sent them, and automated calendar emails should never ask for a reply.

## Problem

A show-rate specialist reported this on 1 Oct (Slack thread). She leaves one voicemail to confirm a booked meeting. For the rest of the sales cycle, every text and email between that lead and the closer shows in her Mine as Unread or Needs reply and adds to her counts.

* She had 57 Needs reply rows, of which 2 were addressed to her.
* Last week each inbound text appeared in the Mine of 4.5 reps on average. 70% of those appearances were for a rep whose number did not receive the text.
* Emails a teammate sent are headed "You", and the list preview starts "You:" on every outgoing message, whoever sent it.
* Most pending Needs reply emails are not from a person at all: 115 of 189 were Calendly notices or calendar invitation replies.

In Close, the tool the team moved from, the Inbox only showed items directed at the rep: their number or their mailbox.

## User experience

* A rep calls a lead to confirm a meeting. The lead later texts the closer's number and emails the closer.
* Today: the lead shows in the first rep's Mine with an unread dot and a Needs reply badge, and adds to the Unread and Needs reply counts and to the Conversations number in the sidebar.
* Expected: the lead is still listed in the first rep's Mine, but is not flagged and adds to no count. The closer, whose number and mailbox received the messages, sees the flags.
* If the lead texts or calls the first rep's own number, or emails their mailbox, it flags for that rep as before.
* An email or text a teammate sent shows the teammate's name, in the open conversation and in the list preview. "You" appears only on your own messages.
* A calendar acceptance or a Calendly notice arriving in a mailbox does not put the person under Needs reply for anyone.

## What's included

* **Flag only what came to you.** In Mine, the unread dot, the Unread and Needs reply tabs, their counts and the Conversations number in the sidebar only include a person when the message came to you.
* **Real sender names.** Sent emails, list previews and call cards name who sent them: "You", the teammate's name, "Name 8", or "Your team".
* **Automated emails never count as Needs reply.** This applies everywhere Needs reply shows, in Mine and Everyone, in every workspace.
* Not included: who is listed in Mine (unchanged from ENG-14540), the order of the Mine list (a separate follow-up), and whether an unanswered call should add a person to Mine (left as is).

## How it should work

* **Came to you** means: a text on your phone number, an email that reached your connected mailbox (to you or copied), or a call or voicemail to you.
* **Needs reply in Mine** shows when the unanswered text or email came to you, or you have been in touch with the person since it arrived.
* **No rep on the receiving end.** A message to a number or mailbox with no current rep flags for everyone who has the person in Mine, as today.
* **Mark unread by hand** keeps working as it does now.
* **Everyone** keeps its per-person Unread and Needs reply. Only the automated email rule changes there.
* **Automated emails** are scheduling and notification emails: Calendly notices, Name 7 Calendar notifications, no-reply and notification senders, and calendar invitations and replies (subjects starting Invitation, Updated invitation, Accepted, Declined, Tentative, Canceled, Proposed new time), whoever's address they come from. They still appear in the conversation and can still be unread. They never set Needs reply and never clear it: a real message that is still waiting stays Needs reply when an automated email arrives after it.
* **Existing people.** Flags already set by automated emails clear at the next nightly repair.
* **Where the "came to you" rule applies.** The AI Acquisition Sales Team's faster Conversations list, the same path as ENG-14540. Other workspaces keep per-person flags until they move to that list.

## Done when

- [ ] A rep who only called a person does not see that person as Unread or Needs reply when the person texts another rep's number or emails another rep's mailbox: not in the list, the tabs, the counts or the sidebar number.
- [ ] The rep whose number or mailbox received the message does see it flagged.
- [ ] A text to a rep's own number, a call to them and an email to their mailbox still flag for that rep.
- [ ] An email, text or call by a teammate shows the teammate's name in the open conversation and in the list preview.
- [ ] A calendar acceptance or Calendly notice does not put a person under Needs reply, and does not remove Needs reply from a real message that is still waiting.
- [ ] The Mine list and its counts stay within the speed reached by the Mine speed fix (about 40 ms for the busiest Sales Team rep).

## Open questions

* Should a declined or cancelled meeting notice still ask for a reply? Recommended default: no. They are calendar notices like the others, and they still show as unread and on the person's timeline.

## Implementation context

* The sender-name work in ENG-14545 covered texts and calls in the open conversation. Email cards and list previews were left out.
* The per-rep times stored for Mine already record when a message last reached each rep, so "came to you" needs no new stored data.
* Point-in-time evidence and design notes: AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Show synced email threads and support replies in Conversations
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Simple summary

**User problem:** Emails synced from Gmail or Microsoft do not yet appear in Conversations, so reps cannot manage the full customer conversation in one place.

**Decision:** This belongs in Conversations, but it must wait for ENG-12256 (mailbox sync) and ENG-12569 (safe sending). Keep it in Backlog until both are complete.

---

## Outcome

Synced Gmail and Microsoft threads appear in Conversations, and authorized users can reply without losing or duplicating sent mail.

## Scope

* Reuse workspace-bound mailbox sync from ENG-12256.
* Reuse safe-send idempotency and reconciliation from ENG-12569.
* List, open, paginate, search and reply to email threads in Conversations.
* Preserve organization membership, record-level permissions, participant privacy and per-user unread state.
* Do not trigger provider imports from read endpoints.

## Dependencies

This ticket cannot complete until ENG-12256 and ENG-12569 are complete. Other ENG-12969 children remain independently schedulable.

## Done when

* Synced Gmail and Microsoft threads appear once in the correct workspace.
* Authorized users can open and reply from Conversations.
* Sending and retries cannot lose or duplicate sent mail.
* Read endpoints do not trigger provider synchronization.
* Restricted participants, messages and snippets do not leak through lists, search, unread counts or exports.
* Focused list, detail, reply, tenancy, permission and idempotency tests pass.

## Notification integration

**Notification and reply-state integration**

Notification links must open the exact authorized mailbox conversation and preserve the sending identity. Viewing/dismissing a notification does not mean the conversation was answered. Apply read and handled state only through the inbound revision actually viewed or addressed. A newer inbound email remains actionable after an older reply's delayed success, stale Done or failure. Provider-accepted send is recorded as sent, not delivered; ambiguous outcomes reconcile before retry. Keep the draft and recovery state visible when sending fails.

### Close guidance

Close emailing and Close Inbox guide replying in context, reconnecting a mailbox and explicit failed-send recovery. Acquisity's workspace authorization remains authoritative.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Show calls and texts from the last 90 days in the Conversations list
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The Conversations list, counts and badge only include people whose latest call or text is from the last 90 days, as email already does. Older history stays on each person's timeline and record Activity tab, and search still finds them.

## Problem

Calls and texts have no time window, so every call ever made, including about 440k imported from Close, stays a permanent inbox entry, and every load processes all of them.

## User experience

A rep opens Conversations: people whose latest call or text is older than 90 days no longer appear in the list. Searching their name, phone or email still finds them, and opening them shows their full history. Nothing changes for anyone active in the last 90 days.

## What's included

* 90-day window on calls and texts in the list, counts, badge and My Day Replies, applied before the per-source work, not after.
* The email window moves before its newest-message lookup too, so old email threads stop costing time.
* Not included: the ready inbox table and switching reads to it (separate tickets under ENG-14368).

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately. It edits the same query files as the badge and shared count work, so rebase onto that once it merges.

## Done when

- [ ] A person whose latest call or text is older than 90 days is not in the list, is found by search, and keeps full history on their timeline.
- [ ] Counts and badge match the list for Mine and Everyone.
- [ ] On the production replica, list and counts are faster than before for the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace.

## Open questions

* 90 days for every channel? Recommended: yes, to match email.

## Implementation context

* AI context.md: where each channel's window is applied today and the suggested change.

relatedSnapshot.title: Read and reply to email threads on the deal and person Emails tab
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

On CRM v2 deal and person pages, the Emails tab is still the older screen: a split view whose right half says "Select an email to view" until you pick a thread. This change shows a simple list of email threads that opens a thread full width in place, using the same email reader as Conversations, so reps can read and reply to a whole thread without leaving the record.

## Problem

Reps open a deal or person to catch up on the email history. Today the tab wastes half its width on an empty pane, shows emails from a different data path than Conversations, and renders them differently, so the same email looks different in the two places.

## User experience

A rep opens a deal or person and chooses the Emails tab:

* They see a list of email threads with everyone on the record: people, subject, a clean preview, message count, attachment mark, time and a Needs reply mark.
* All, AI SDR and Human filters appear only when the record has AI SDR threads, plus an Unread filter.
* Clicking a thread opens it full width in place: subject, people, Done and snooze, newer and older thread arrows, Expand all, older messages folded to one line, the latest open, and Reply, Reply all and Forward on each message.
* Replies are written inline under the thread. Back returns to the list.
* An empty record says where emails come from and points to the composer below.

## What's included

* Deal and person pages in CRM v2. Company pages keep no Emails tab.
* The same email card, formatting, quote folding and sanitising as ENG-14349.
* The same permission rules as Conversations for who can read which emails.
* New emails still start from the record's docked composer; the tab adds no second New email button.

## Done when

* The v2 deal and person Emails tab lists the record's email threads and opens a thread full width in place, with Back to the list.
* Each message renders with the shared email reader; replies send from the inline composer and appear in the thread.
* AI SDR and Human filters show only when AI SDR threads exist.
* Viewers see exactly the emails Conversations lets them see.
* Checked in light and dark, desktop and phone widths.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Sync rep inboxes automatically
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Closed 25 Sep 2026. The Gmail half is complete. Microsoft 365 sync continues in ENG-12972, and its last open piece is ENG-13964. Live QA for both providers is tracked in the completion checklist of ENG-13574.**

## Overview

Import recent email history and keep connected Gmail and Microsoft 365 inboxes updated automatically.

This is the provider-sync sub-master. Provider-specific implementation stays in separate tickets so each integration can be built and verified properly.

## Problem

CRM can sync a provider thread when it already knows the thread ID, but it does not discover and continuously ingest a mailbox. Opening the Emails tab currently fills part of this gap by searching the provider and writing results into CRM.

## Proposed fix

Build background ingestion for:

* Gmail.
* Microsoft 365.

Both use the workspace binding from ENG-12668 and the same normalized CRM persistence path.

## What's included

* A fixed recent Inbox and Sent window.
* No drafts, spam or trash.
* Provider message and conversation identifiers.
* Existing supported bodies, participants, timestamps and attachment metadata.
* Idempotent notifications and jobs.
* Cursor advancement only after persistence.
* Safe retry, disconnect and workspace mismatch handling.
* Delayed and reconnect-required account states.

## Child tickets

This ticket is a checkpoint. The actual code ships under the tickets below, one PR per ticket. Status as of 25 Sep 2026.

**Gmail**

1. Keep Gmail conversations up to date automatically (ENG-2061, Done). The Gmail umbrella. All three of its pieces below are Done.
   1. Import recent Gmail history into CRM (ENG-13525, Done). One-off background import of the last 90 days of Inbox and Sent mail.
   2. Make new Gmail messages arrive in CRM automatically (ENG-13528, Done). Gmail tells us when something changed and we pull the change in, so new mail shows up without anyone opening a page.
   3. Show Gmail sync health and finish disconnect cleanup (ENG-13529, Done). Account settings show importing, healthy or reconnect needed, and disconnecting stops Gmail from notifying us. Live Gmail QA happens here.

**Microsoft 365**

2. Keep Microsoft 365 conversations up to date automatically (ENG-12972, Todo, parked). The same three steps as Gmail, for Outlook, now split into the tickets below.
   1. Import recent Outlook history into CRM (ENG-13961, Done).
   2. Make new Outlook mail arrive in CRM automatically (ENG-13962, Done).
   3. Recover Outlook sync from stale delta tokens and handle removed messages (ENG-13963, Done).
   4. Show Outlook sync health and finish disconnect cleanup (ENG-13964, Backlog, parked). Also carries the Outlook half of the Emails tab clean-up and the real Microsoft 365 mailbox check.

**Shared clean-up**

3. Stop opening the Emails tab from importing Gmail data (ENG-12690, Done). The Gmail half is done. The Outlook half moved to ENG-13964 above.

**Still open**

The Microsoft 365 leg. The Done when boxes below were not re-checked in this refresh.

**Order**

Gmail first (1.1, then 1.2, then 1.3). Microsoft can start once 1.1 is merged, because it reuses the same way of saving messages. The Emails tab clean-up goes last, after both providers keep CRM current on their own.

## Blocked by

* Connect one mailbox to the right workspace. Done on 15 Sep 2026, so this ticket is no longer blocked.

## How it should work

Gmail uses watch notifications and history cursors. Microsoft uses Graph subscriptions and separate Inbox and Sent delta cursors. Provider code may differ, but both must produce the same CRM outcome and safety guarantees.

## Who can do what

Only an active bound mailbox can import. Every job rechecks the binding, generation and current workspace access.

## What the user sees

Email appears in CRM automatically. Account settings show healthy, delayed, disconnected or reconnect-required state.

## Done when

- [ ] Gmail and Microsoft pass the shared behaviour.
- [ ] Initial and continuous sync use background jobs.
- [ ] Page views are not required to discover messages.
- [ ] Replay produces one CRM message.
- [ ] Cursor recovery is tested.
- [ ] Live QA passes with one Gmail and one Microsoft mailbox.

## Open questions

None beyond the bounded provider questions in each child.

## Expected outcome

Different providers produce one reliable CRM inbox experience.

## Twenty reference and implementation detail

Use Twenty CRM as a product and architecture reference. Verify the current source when implementation starts. Learn from its sync boundaries, state machines and user experience, then reimplement the behaviour in Acquisity's Next.js, tRPC, Drizzle and Inngest stack.

Do not copy Twenty application code verbatim or introduce a dependency on Twenty-hosted services. Twenty's core application is AGPL-licensed, so this ticket is about learning from the design and creating an Acquisity-native implementation.

Model one provider-neutral lifecycle: initial import, catch-up/replay, live, delayed, reconnect required and disconnected. Notifications only enqueue work. Provider history or delta APIs remain the source of truth. Commit a cursor or checkpoint only after the corresponding CRM writes succeed. Replayed jobs, overlapping notifications and the sent-email reconciliation path must converge on one stored message. Provider deletion events must be handled explicitly rather than leaving permanently stale CRM data.

relatedSnapshot.title: Conversations reuses the sidebar's unread count instead of counting again
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

In CRM v2, the sidebar's Conversations unread count and the Unread and Needs reply counts on the Conversations page become one shared count. Opening Conversations reuses a fresh sidebar count instead of rebuilding the workspace's whole history a second time. The numbers reps see don't change.

## Problem

Every Conversations count rebuilds every call, text and email in the workspace, which takes about 0.3 seconds today for the AI Acquisition Sales Team and grows with history. The CRM v2 sidebar count added by ENG-14327 asks for Mine unread every minute on every dashboard page. Opening Conversations then asks for the same Mine count again, keyed slightly differently, so the same history is built twice for one answer. The Close import will make each build much slower.

## User experience

A rep sees the unread count beside Conversations in the sidebar and opens Conversations. The page's Unread chip shows the same number straight away, from the count the sidebar already has, if it is under 30 seconds old. When the rep reads a conversation, marks it done or sends a reply, the sidebar and the chips both update at once, as they do today. Changing to Everyone or a single channel still loads its own count.

## What's included

* The sidebar count and the Conversations page's default Mine count use one shared cached count, kept fresh for up to 30 seconds.
* A rep's own read, unread, done and send actions still refresh every count straight away.
* Tests showing the sidebar number equals the page's Unread count for Mine and Everyone.
* A before and after count of how many times the history is built when Conversations opens.
* Not included: today's CRM tab badge in workspaces without CRM v2. It stays as it is, because moving it would hide it there and change what it counts. Also not included: the 90-day window (ENG-14369), the inbox table, person timeline speed and the Close importer.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14327 (Acquisity/Acquisity#6636) must merge first, because it adds the sidebar count.

## Done when

- [ ] In a CRM v2 workspace, opening Conversations with a sidebar count under 30 seconds old makes no second count request, and the chip matches the sidebar.
- [ ] Reading, marking done and sending update the sidebar and the chips immediately.
- [ ] Tests prove the sidebar count and the page's Unread count agree for Mine and Everyone.
- [ ] Workspaces without CRM v2 see no change to the CRM tab badge.

## Implementation context

* The server path is unchanged: both reads already use the fast person count from ENG-14300.
* A per-user server cache was considered and not chosen (James, 28 Sep): the sidebar polls every 60 seconds, so a 15 to 30 second server cache would rarely be hit, and it would add Redis to this path.
* Separate from the 2 second server wait on every page (ENG-14322).

relatedSnapshot.title: Reply to texts and manage unread
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Audit update (2026-09-01; verified against origin/main **`b56300e23152`**):** The native Name 12 status and blocker relations now reflect the verified current scope. Existing description history is preserved below.

## Overview

A rep can continue an SMS conversation and manage their own read state without leaving Conversations.

## Problem

Current read state can be shared across the workspace, and SMS reply behavior is not integrated into the new Conversations screen. Email reliability work should not block the SMS MVP.

## Proposed fix

Add per-user CRM read state and connect the composer to the existing authorized SMS send-and-record path.

## What's included

* Per-user read and unread.
* CRM-local unread counts.
* Needs reply for SMS when the latest customer message has no later outbound response.
* Reply from an authorized phone number for the conversation.
* Sending, sent and failed states.
* Durable recording through the existing SMS path.
* Idempotent retry.

Not included: email display, email replies, bulk actions, generated replies, forwarding, reassignment or cadence management.

## Blocked by

* Build the all-activity Conversations screen.

## How it should work

* Read state is keyed to workspace, user and conversation.
* Opening may mark read for that user only.
* Mark unread persists through refresh.
* Needs reply is independent from unread.
* The server validates the real sending phone number.
* Successful sends appear once.
* Failed sends keep the draft and show retry.
* Retrying the same operation cannot send twice.

## Who can do what

A user may reply only when they can view the conversation and use its sender. Every read and write is workspace scoped.

## What the user sees

Read controls, counts, the SMS composer, disconnected-sender state, and sending, success or failure feedback. Email controls are absent.

## Done when

- [ ] Two users can hold different read states.
- [ ] Refresh does not overwrite CRM-local state.
- [ ] Needs reply matches the agreed SMS rule.
- [ ] SMS uses the correct sender.
- [ ] Success appears once.
- [ ] Retry cannot duplicate a text.
- [ ] Browser QA covers read, unread, needs reply, success, failure and disconnected sender.
- [ ] Permission and cross-workspace tests cover every mutation.

## Open questions

None: V1 is SMS only and keeps read state local.

## Expected outcome

Reps can work SMS conversations without false success, duplicate sends or shared unread state.

## Notification integration

**Notification and reply-state integration**

Personal notification read/dismiss state is separate from CRM per-user unread and shared Needs reply. Advance the user's read watermark only through content actually rendered in a focused, visible conversation. A send or Done action records the inbound revision it covers. If inbound A is followed by a pending reply and then inbound B, a delayed success or stale Done for A must leave B actionable. Queued/unknown send state is not proof of delivery; a later terminal failure creates action-required work without erasing newer inbound activity.

### Close guidance

Close SMS and MMS and Close Inbox guide direct text replies and read versus handled behavior. The covered-inbound revision requirement prevents newer replies being hidden.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: CRM v2 Conversations: emails in the inbox, one row per person
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

In the v2 Conversations inbox, emails with people in the CRM join texts and calls, and each person appears once in the list with their latest message across every channel. Reps get per-rep unread and needs-reply for email, and can Mark done.

## Problem

Today Conversations lists only texts and calls, one row per text thread and one per call. Email, the main channel with most contacts, lives only on record pages. Email volume is large (6.78 million threads platform-wide, 4,830 contact-linked Gmail threads in the pilot workspace), so the inbox needs clear rules on which email counts before it can be shown.

## User experience

* The channel menu gains Emails. Each person is one row; the preview, time and channel mark come from their latest item on any channel.
* A person is unread when any of their visible sources is unread. Email counts as unread only when it arrived after the rep last opened that person and within the last 7 days, or when the rep marked it unread.
* A person needs a reply when their latest text or email is inbound, under 14 days old and not an out-of-office. Calls never set it. Mark done clears it until they write again.
* "Mine" means the rep owns the contact. Rows with no contact (unknown numbers) keep today's rule, the phone line's assignee.
* Counts include email under the same rules.

## What's included

* Email threads that are linked to a CRM contact, from Gmail, Outlook or manual entry, whose last message is within 90 days. The person's thread still shows their full email history.
* Left out: email from people not in the CRM, and cold-campaign (Company One) threads, which the AI SDR inbox owns.
* One additive read-state migration: per-rep read state for email threads, and a person-level row holding Mark done. Opening a person marks all their visible sources read in one step.
* Any new index goes in its own small change first, chosen from the final query plan on the read replica.
* Gmail first. Outlook follows ENG-12972 (Microsoft 365 live sync).
* This is the v2 home of ENG-13342; agree with Elis whether that ticket carries the implementation.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14165 (the v2 Conversations screen).

## Who can do what

Email rows need thread-view permission and access to the contact under the existing owner scope, the same rule as the record Emails tab. The preview is hidden without email-content permission. Access follows the contact, not the mailbox, as it does on records today.

## Done when

* The pilot workspace sees contact emails in the v2 list, one row per person, with texts and calls folded in.
* Unread, needs-reply and Mark done follow the rules above, per rep.
* Restricted emails and previews never appear through the list, search or counts.
* With `CRM v2` off, today's Conversations page and query are unchanged.
* The final list query is measured on the replica for the pilot workspace and the largest contact-linked workspace, with the plan recorded on the PR.

## Design

* Design (full kit): Acquisity v2 Kit, Conversations, route `#/screen/crm-conversations`.
* Production cut: see ENG-14165. This ticket un-gates the list parts marked for it.
* The design artifacts are private until James shares them.

## Implementation context

High risk: list query rewrite, a read-state migration and a cursor version bump. The data rules and rollback notes are in the Conversations parity plan, section 2, which James holds.

relatedSnapshot.title: CRM v2 Conversations: filters on one line, channel menu icons and kit polish
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

On production, the Conversations inbox drifts from the kit design in several places. The worst are the filter row breaking onto a second line and a channel menu that looks unfinished. This ticket brings the list, thread header, timeline and contact panel in line with the production-cut design.

## Problem

* On a busy workspace, the unread and needs-reply counts show "99+". That makes the All / Unread / Needs reply and Mine / Everyone controls too wide for the list. Picking Everyone bolds its label and pushes the pair onto its own row.
* The "All channels" menu has an empty gap on the left, no mark on the selected channel and no icons. The call outcome menu on a call has the same empty gap.
* Other spots are off-design: the thread title is too small, messages sit evenly spaced with no width cap on wide screens, the list shows plain grey blocks while loading, and a failed load replaces the screen with a bare Retry. Several action buttons also have no icons.

## User experience

A rep opens Conversations. Filters sit on one line at any list width; if the rep drags the list narrow, the counts drop out before anything wraps. The channel menu shows an icon for each channel and a check on the current one. Threads read like the kit: a larger title, grouped message spacing and a centred column on wide screens. Loading says what is happening, and a failed load keeps the layout with a clear "Try again".

## What's included

* The filter row stays on one line. The list's minimum width rises so the labels always fit.
* Channel and call outcome menus: icons, a selected check, no empty gutter, and the kit's small grey section label.
* Thread title size, the More button style and tooltip, and icons on Contact details, Mark as unread, Retry and Load more.
* Message spacing and a width cap. Type chips get icons, and a second click on a chip returns to All.
* List loading skeleton with words, an inline error card, no empty unread pill, and the empty-selection copy.

Not included:

* The composer: attachments work is in flight in feat(crm): Twilio text attachments in Conversations, gated by CRM v2 (ENG-13826).
* Dark surfaces and the page frame, which ENG-14279 owns.
* The scheduled-count badge, which ENG-14171 owns.
* Changes to shared menu and filter components.
* The deal stage pill colour. A stage's colour comes from its place in its pipeline, which the contact panel does not load, and a partial version would disagree with the Deals board.
* Load speed, which has its own ticket.

## Done when

* With "99+" counts, the filter row stays on one line at the default list width with either Mine or Everyone selected, and at the narrowest list width.
* The channel menu shows icons and a check on the selected channel. The call outcome menu has no empty gutter.
* A browser check against the production-cut kit at 1440 / 1650 / 1920 and phone width, in light and dark, is recorded on the PR, with each remaining difference fixed or explained.

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix the older-notification backfill for people with an older message never read
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The one-off job that links people's older Name 2 notifications to their source still fails for a few people: anyone with an older message they never read. This fixes that and re-checks those people, so the full report is complete before the real run.

## Problem

After ENG-14572 fixed the batch size in Acquisity/Acquisity#6775, a full report-only run finished in production on 2 October 2026. It covered 8,971 people and wrote nothing. 11 people (0.1%) still failed with `provider_read_failed`, so their older items are not counted, and a real run would leave them on Name 2.

The cause: Name 2 answers the older-message read normally, but the Name 2 library we use rejects its answer when a message has never been read. Name 2 sends "last read" as empty for those messages, and the library only accepts a date. A read-only check against production reproduced it for three of the 11 people.

## Proposed fix

1. Accept older messages that were never read, without loosening any other check on Name 2's answer.
2. After deploy, run the report-only pass again for just the 11 people and add their results to the report.

## What's included

* The older-message read used by the backfill job.
* A report-only re-run for the 11 people, and the full report summary posted on this ticket.
* Excludes: the escalations with no matching run (not yet ticketed), any match or left-behind rule change, the real (writing) run, and ENG-13839 step D.

## How it should work

* A message with no "last read" date is read like any other. The same identity checks still decide whether it can be linked.
* Any other unexpected answer from Name 2 still fails that person safely with `provider_read_failed`.
* Everything else stays as shipped: report-only by default, one person at a time, nothing sent, nothing written to Name 2.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: an internal job run by engineering, with no new access.

## What the user sees

Nothing directly. After the real run, these 11 people are no longer held on Name 2 because of this read.

## Done when

* The 11 people re-run in report-only mode with no `provider_read_failed` from this cause.
* A test covers an older message whose "last read" date is empty.
* The full report, including the 11, is posted on this ticket.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Everyone with older items is counted, so the real run can be scheduled on a complete report.

## Implementation context

* Report-only results, 2 October 2026, 8,971 people, 0 receipts written:
  * Would be linked: 7,737 AI SDR escalations and about 7,190 campaign alerts, for 785 people.
  * Left behind: 122,979 overdue reminders with no delivery record, about 8,500 older Done items, 165 retired usage-limit alerts.
  * Still blocked: 32,450 escalations with no matching run (1,055 people), 2,855 items whose campaign is missing, 412 escalations whose finished source can't be proven.
  * 838 people have no Name 2 account and 8,106 haven't opted in to the new list.
* The read is `retrieveLegacyMessages` in `apps/web/lib/notifications/provider/novu-legacy-messages.ts`, calling `novu.messages.retrieve`.
* AI context.md holds the production evidence, root cause, where to find the 11 people, and test seams as of 2 October 2026.
